questions.question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses well in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more time and distance to stop than smaller vehicles. If you stop suddenly in front of a large vehicle, the driver may not be able to stop in time and could crash into you.

questions.question: What risk does fatigue increase?

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows your decision-making and reaction time, raising your crash risk. You could fall asleep behind the wheel, which could injure or kill you or others.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unfit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unfit to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can reduce your ability to drive safely. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, alcohol's effects will only go away by:

options.text: Taking a cold shower.
Waiting several hours.
Drinking several cups of coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Waiting several hours.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Cold showers, coffee, or exercise will not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before moving your vehicle left or right to alert other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before any lane change.

questions.question: You must obey instructions from school crossing guards:

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Unless you do not see any children.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always watch for crossing guards near schools and follow their instructions.

questions.question: When driving through work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed throughout the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a work zone and be prepared to stop. Follow posted speed limits and stay alert. Workers may be present in the area.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness and concentration.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness and concentration, slows your reaction time, and badly reduces your coordination.

questions.question: Driving while taking medication that impairs your driving is allowed:

options.text: Never.
If you don't feel drowsy.
If it is prescribed by a doctor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that impairs your driving. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: When taking any medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor about how it affects your driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive more slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about how it affects your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can reduce your ability to drive. Always talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how a medicine will affect your driving. This is especially important for tranquilizers or sedatives.

questions.question: What is this bicyclist signaling?

options.text: A left turn.
An upcoming stop.
A right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A left turn.
questions.explanation: Bicycles do not have turn signals. Bicyclists use their arms and hands to signal. A straight left arm means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: Which of these substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can make it unsafe to drive. These include tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough syrups and cold medicines, and illegal drugs. Some of these substances contain alcohol, codeine, or antihistamines that affect driving.

questions.question: What does a steady green traffic light mean?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can go through the intersection. Always yield to traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area where road construction workers work.
The area where pedestrians can cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians can cross the street.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are marked with white lines to show where pedestrians can cross. Some crosswalks have extra lines between them. Crosswalks can also be unmarked.

questions.question: The golden rule of driving is to:

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive aggressively.
Treat others the way you want to be treated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat others the way you want to be treated.
questions.explanation: The golden rule of driving is to treat other drivers the way you want to be treated. Follow traffic laws, drive safely, and avoid taking risks that could hurt you or others.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get to your destination faster.
Turn up your radio.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue: struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting out of your lane, or needing to turn up the radio to stay awake. If you notice these signs, stop at a safe place and rest.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left then right.
The road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road will curve right, then curve left. Slow down to safely handle the curves ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve.
Drive no slower than 35 mph through the curve.
Go 35 mph or slower around the curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go 35 mph or slower around the curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert you to dangers just ahead. A speed plaque under the sign tells you what speed to use for that section of road.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Stare directly ahead at the road.
Only focus on the middle of the road.
Watch all around your car: beside, ahead, and behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch all around your car: beside, ahead, and behind.
questions.explanation: Watch all around your car. Good drivers know what is happening everywhere around their vehicle.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep cars out of dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep cars out of dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Look for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. These warn you and show you where to go.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to move out of an aggressive driver's way. Do not compete with other drivers. Always follow traffic rules and cooperate with other road users to prevent crashes.

questions.question: Which statement about changing lanes is true?

options.text: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for all lane changes.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check all mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles are in the next lane.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Low visibility at night makes it hard to judge distance and how fast other cars are traveling. You can only see as far as your headlights reach.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, what must you do?

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. You must stop for pedestrians whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked. Pedestrians must obey traffic signals.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes and is in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Proceed if you have the right-of-way.
Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian crosses the street before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian crosses the street before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection. Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before you move forward.
